name: divergence-lt-as-min
note: FCB-ONLY SEMANTICS: in FCB's bespoke engine '<' means MIN, so MIN(3,5) = 3. expression-kit/EvalEx treats '<' as a boolean less-than comparison: 3 < 5 is TRUE, and DefaultFormulaEngine coerces the BOOLEAN result to a number via EvaluationValue.getNumberValue() (TRUE -> 1). So EvalEx returns 1, NOT FCB's 3. This fixture asserts EvalEx's ACTUAL behavior (evaluates without error, yields 1) to DOCUMENT the divergence; it does NOT assert FCB parity. expectedResult=1 here records the EvalEx-observed value, not the FCB value (which would be 3).
